summary: An air unit and a police dog helped search a business yard in the 5800 block of South Union Avenue after a call about a possible unreported stolen vehicle with a firearm on the seat. A man was found hiding under a fifth-wheel trailer and one person was taken into custody.
A crew was sent to the 800 block of East Brundage Lane for difficulty breathing.
A white box truck was reported driving in and out of lanes at high speed on southbound Interstate 5 north of Highway 156.
A crew was sent to the Navigation Center on East Brundage Lane for a maternity call.
Crews were sent to a commercial fire alarm at a plant on Lerdo Highway and canceled a second engine.
Officers were sent to the 3300 block of Bernard Street for seven people reported to be wearing ski masks; no weapons were seen.
Officers were sent to the 9300 block of Caminos Street for an open phone line where a child was heard telling someone to stop hitting his mother.
A crew was sent to the 6100 block of Panorama Drive for difficulty breathing.
Officers checked on a man reported to be yelling in an alley off the 1100 block of 3rd Street.
A trailer came off a dolly and ran off the road into a parked car at a charging station. No one was hurt and crews worked to secure the charging equipment.
A hit-and-run crash with moderate to major injuries was reported at 8:34 p.m. The car that fled was described as a black Toyota sedan heading east.
Officers were sent to the 800 block of Beardsley Avenue for a juvenile reported to be suicidal and holding a knife.
Officers were sent to the 22500 block of Sidding Road for a man knocking on doors asking for food and water after he was asked to leave a gas station.

Two people cut through a razor-wire fence and got into a business yard. Units set a perimeter and a police dog and an air unit joined the search. One of the two was reported hurt getting over the wire.

Officers were sent to the 2300 block of Haven Avenue on a burglary call that turned out to be a fight between roommates. One of them, a woman, was armed with a sword. Officers noted a January case at the address involving a firearm.
Officers checked a vacant lot in the 8500 block of Dawn Street, where two men were reported on the property and vehicles and utility trailers were stored.

Officers were sent to Kentucky Street and Bale at 9:26 p.m. for seven juveniles reported in the area. One of them was said to have a firearm and was last seen walking south toward the railroad tracks.
Units used a heat signature to find someone under a trailer in the 3500 block of Brian Way and staged medics while they worked to reach them.
Officers were sent to the 700 block of Brundage Lane for a man reported to be jumping on a vehicle he shared with the caller.
A man flagged down a crew at a gas station on Mettler Frontage Road West. He appeared to be in a mental health crisis and said he was on his way to family he believed were being hurt.
A crew was sent to a commercial fire alarm in the 3900 block of East Brundage Lane.
Officers checked on a woman who made suicidal statements and said she had taken pills. There was no answer at the door.
A crew was sent to the 4200 block of Jaspar Avenue for a seizure.
A pursuit ran eastbound on Edison Highway at 11:40 p.m., past Sterling and then Fairfax, at speeds from 85 to 120 mph. An air unit was launching.

disposition: on foot northbound on Fillmore Street
summary: Officers were sent at 11:45 p.m. for a man with a machete riding a black bicycle westbound on Cedar Street toward Lincoln. He was later reported on foot northbound on Fillmore Street from Cedar.
Deputies were sent at 12:11 a.m. to check on someone reported to be having suicidal thoughts at a home on Sierra Highway.
Officers checked the area of the 100 block of Hart Street for a man heard screaming for help near the canal.
A crew found a smoldering charcoal grill left unattended in a garage after a fire alarm. The house was evacuated and there was no fire.
Officers were sent to an apartment on 33rd Street where a woman who first asked for medical help was talking about wanting to die and scissors were mentioned. It was not known whether she was armed.
A crew was sent to the 200 block of Hudson Drive for a cardiac arrest after a seizure. The patient was reported to not be breathing.
A crew was sent to the 3100 block of Monterey Street for difficulty breathing.
A crew was sent to the 16300 block of Clarisse Street for a medical alarm.
Officers were sent to the 5900 block of Country View Lane, where a woman was reported to be armed with a brick and threatening the caller. She had put the brick down by the time officers reached her.
A resident's camera recorded someone taking packages from his porch and from the area on Kathleen Avenue. He put his loss at $500 to $1,000 and described a gray extended-cab pickup.
Officers and a crew were sent to the 900 block of Lake Street for a man reported to have relapsed on fentanyl and stopped answering. The call was updated to an overdose.
A crew was sent to a gas station on Mettler Frontage Road West for a fall, then upgraded the call: the patient had a head wound and was confused.
Two engines and medics were sent to the 6300 block of Victor Street for an unconscious patient, and the call was upgraded to a cardiac arrest.
Officers checked the 8100 block of Edison Highway for a van reported to be parked at a gas station. No one was seen.
A truck driver hauling hay westbound on Highway 46 west of Highway 33 told his employer that vehicles were passing and tailgating him.

Officers were sent to the 4800 block of Columbus Street, where a mother was reported to have locked her two-year-old in a bedroom, started using cocaine and fallen asleep. The child was still in the room.
Vehicle crash near Tesla station off I-5 and 46.
Traffic collision involving smaller vehicle and pickup.
Pedestrian hit by fleeing pickup in Taft.
Truck crash reported on Gosford Road.
Cardiac arrest with CPR in progress at Buena Vista.
